title: Can a rectangle be named with its corners in any order?
description: A rectangle with corners A, B, C and D is named by walking round its edge. The video finds the names that are allowed and the names that are not. Keeko raises the doubt that any order of the letters will do.
teaching_notes: One idea: a name lists the corners in order going round the shape, so every two letters side by side are the ends of one side. Watch for children who jump across the middle along a diagonal.

source: A rectangle ABCD has corners A (top left), B (top right), C (bottom right), D (bottom left). Besides ABCD it can be named BCDA, CDAB, DABC, ADCB, DCBA, CBAD and BADC. Can a rectangle be named using any combination of the labels around its corners? What names are allowed and what names are not?
video_script.why: The child learns that a name for a rectangle lists its corners in order going round, so neighbouring letters are the ends of a side.
video_script.substitution: The names ABDC and ACBD tested against the rule of neighbouring letters.
video_script.anchor: A rectangle ABCD with A at the top left, B at the top right, C at the bottom right and D at the bottom left
video_script.wrong_answer: any order of the letters will do
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks any order of the letters will do, because all four letters are there. The name ACBD goes from A across the middle to C, which is a diagonal and not a side, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: A rectangle is named by its corners in order going round it.

final_answer.value: No; ABDC and ACBD are not allowed; a name lists the corners in order going round the rectangle, starting from any corner and going in either direction
final_answer.spoken: no, eigh B D C and eigh C B D are not allowed; a rectangle is named by its corners in order going round it, from any corner and either way

hold_back: ABDC and ACBD are not allowed
never_show: the verdict on the names before the answer
maths_rules: Rectangle ABCD: A top left, B top right, C bottom right, D bottom left; the sides are AB, BC, CD, DA.
Valid names go round in order: ABCD, BCDA, CDAB, DABC one way and ADCB, DCBA, CBAD, BADC the other way.
Rule: every two letters side by side in a name are the two ends of one side.
ABDC is not valid: B and D are opposite corners, so BD is a diagonal. ACBD is not valid: A and C are opposite corners, so AC is a diagonal.
Check: BCDA uses BC, CD, DA, which are all sides.
video_script.design: One idea: neighbouring letters in a name must be the ends of a side. Wrong idea: any order of the letters is fine. The rectangle stays all video.
